CHALLENGE C0025 | The finding incorrectly states verification fails for chains WITHOUT epochs. In fact, chains without epochs SUCCEED because export_bundle falls back to computing the merkle_root from raw_records, matching build_inclusion_proof. The actual bug is that chains WITH epochs and unsealed records will fail, because export_bundle uses epochs[-1]["merkle_root"] while build_inclusion_proof computes proofs against all records.

DESCRIPTION: FIND: In `verify_bundle` (bench/evidence.py), the method iterates through `zip(bundle.records, bundle.inclusion_proofs)` and validates the cryptographic proofs against the bundle's Merkle root, but completely fails to verify that the raw `record` matches the `proof`. Specifically, an attacker can tamper with `record["sealed_body"]` (e.g., changing the payload) while leaving the valid `proof` unmodified. Since `verify_bundle` never asserts that the unverified `record` mathematically hashes to the trusted `proof["chain_hash"]`, the tampered record will be silently authenticated as valid. Evidence: lines 415-424 show `record` is only used to extract a sequence number for error reporting, not for any cryptographic checks.
FOLLOW: If external auditors rely on `verify_bundle` to validate exported `EvidenceBundle` packages, they will accept completely fabricated evidence records. The core objective of the evidence layer (providing verifiable proofs of reasoning) is bypassed.

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.9
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.7
DESCRIPTION: FIND: In `export_bundle`, when `self._chain.epochs` exists, `merkle_root` is assigned to `epochs[-1]["merkle_root"]`. However, the inclusion proofs are generated using `self._chain.build_inclusion_proof(i)`, which ALWAYS computes the proof against all currently appended records (`self._records`). If there are unsealed records appended after the last epoch was sealed, the proof's Merkle tree size will be larger than the epoch's Merkle tree size. This guarantees a mismatch between `proof["merkle_root"]` and `bundle.merkle_root`, causing `verify_bundle` to deterministically fail for any exported bundle on a chain with unsealed records. Evidence: lines 330-337.
FOLLOW: Bundles exported during an active experiment (where unsealed records exist) will fail verification externally, making the audit feature unusable until an epoch is explicitly sealed.
